"I admit that I felt that way."
"I admit that I said that about you."
"I agree with you. I said that."
"I admit that I did that."
"I admit that I was wrong."
"I apologize for saying that."
"I apologize for speaking to you that way."
"I apologize for telling my friends that"
"I apologize for embarrassing you."
"I apologize for leaving you out."
"I apologize for being late."
"Thank you for letting me know how you feel."
"Thank you for opening up to me."
"Thank you for being honest with me."
"Thank you for listening."
"I appreciate you being here for me."
"Thank you for making me feel safe with you."
"I commit-to-change the way I talk about you to other people."
"I commit to be on time"
"I commit-to-change by including you."
"I commit to call you when I say I will."
"I have decided not to say that anymore"
"It's important to me that you feel special, so I commit to not doing that any more."
"Please forgive me."
"Please excuse my behavior."
"I'm asking you to forgive me."
"Please know that I would love your forgiveness."
"Please consider forgiving me."
"Is there anything else bothering you?"
"Please tell me more."
"Help me to understand."
"Help me to understand what you're thinking."
"Help me to know your feelings better."
"So you feel left out and want me to invite you next time?"
"So you felt like I didn't pay any attention to you and want me to include you more?"
"So you are feeling angry because I didn't follow through, and would like for me to do what I say I'm going to do?"
"So you felt abandoned when I left early, and want me to wait for you?"
"So you felt unloved when I said that and want me to think before I speak?"
"So you felt sad to experience that, and want me to change the way I handle those situations?"
"I know how you feel, I have felt the same way before, but what I'm finding out is that I'm not very good about remembering birthdays and I..."
"I know how you feel, I felt scared at first too, but what I found out was that I just didn't know how to express myself to you."
"I know how you felt, I have felt unloved before too, but what I'm finding out is that I need to show you that I care."
"I know how you must feel, I have felt angry about those things too, but what I'm finding out is that I was just afraid, and I didn't need to be. Neith..."
"I understand how you feel. I have felt the same way but what I found out is that we all want the same things."
"I gotcha. I am seeing how you feel. I have felt that way too, but what I'm finding out is there is a solution."
"I appreciate you sharing that."
"Thank you for sharing."
"I appreciate you being honest with me."
"I appreciate you and feel much closer to you now that you shared that with me "
"Thank you for your openness."
"I appreciate everything about you."
"Face each other and match each others' breath while breathing slowly."
"Look each other in the eye and hold the gaze for 10 seconds at a time. Repeat 4 times."
"Stand and slow dance together."
"Give each other a shoulder or back massage."
"Share 5 things that each appreciates about the other."
"Listen to music that both people enjoy."
Notice that he never blamed her, shamed her, felt entitled or was defensive when He apologized.
He simply apologized.
Never say the following when apologizing:
1. I'm sorry, BUT...
2. I'm sorry YOU FEEL THAT WAY.
3. "I'm sorry IF I HURT YOUR FEELINGS"
4. "I'm sorry THAT I MAY HAVE HURT YOU"
The statements above invalidate the apology and actually make the situation worse.
Sometimes we're afraid to be confronted, but if we use these 10 steps and ask for clarification, we're able to connect on a deeper level.
By using these specific "Love Chat" messages, she will melt in your arms and will not be defensive because you are only expressing your feelings (taking 100% responsibility for your feeling).
She will feel safe with you when you express yourself this way.
